meta.title: Temperature control with dead time: why lag causes oscillation
meta.tools: First-order-plus-dead-time (FOPDT) oven model, delay-line simulation, Nyquist/phase-crossover analysis
meta.summary: Control an oven whose heater acts through a 20 s transport delay; predict the proportional gain at which the loop oscillates and the oscillation period from the phase-crossover condition, and find both by simulation.
meta.problem: Why does turning up the gain on a slow thermal system make it oscillate, and how high can it go?
meta.theory:
$G(s)=\frac{K e^{-\theta s}}{\tau s+1}$ with K = 2 °C/%, τ = 200 s, θ = 20 s. Phase crossover: $-\arctan(\omega\tau)-\omega\theta=-\pi$ → ω_u; ultimate gain
$K_u=\frac{\sqrt{1+(\omega_u\tau)^2}}{K}$, oscillation period $2\pi/\omega_u$. The delay's phase −ωθ grows without bound, so every such loop has a finite K_u.
meta.method:
Delay implemented as a sample FIFO (0.1 s steps). P gains swept; K_u found as the gain where the oscillation neither grows nor decays (log-decrement
= 0, bisection).
